# R278 — v0.1.43 pristine tuning gap on the supplied long-input runs

Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only comparison of the pristine official source at `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d` and the supplied 32K receipts. No source edits, builds, tests, GPU/model runs, Git operations, or process operations were performed. Only this report was written.

## Decision

The current settings are not established as optimized. The supplied measurements are useful diagnostics and show the route works on this setup, but every measured row has one sample with tracing/validation enabled and `performance_eligible=false`. The cache-128/cache-512 rows use the same input, binary, environment, and boot, but generated IDs and reported LP5 differ. The source-level search remains incomplete and no best setting can be selected. Prefill and decode must be selected independently: one cache change moved the reported rates in opposite directions, and it also changed output/route placement.

The supplied v160 JSON gives cache128 at 19.070 prefill / 6.295 decode tok/s and cache512 at 17.773 / 8.480, each from a single diagnostic row. Those values must not be used as speed rankings or as a claim of quality-equivalent output. The report marks both rows ineligible, and explicitly says optimization is incomplete. The v156 receipt repeats the cache128 recipe, not an additional clean settings arm. At least 32K inputs are the useful target; short-input or default-startup checks would not answer this search question.

The source-reported safe runtime/compiler stack and the run's build identity must stay distinct. The provided v160 argv/environment and UPDATE_RESULTS identify the measured pristine binary as built with Intel oneAPI 2026.1 `icpx`; that is not the current source-built DPC++/SYCL 7.1.1, Clang 22, libSYCL ABI 9 stack, and neither is interchangeable with oneAPI 2025.1.1. The v160 outcomes cannot be relabeled as a measurement on either of those other stacks. Pick one exact safe stack, record its compiler/runtime/device identity, and establish its own matched control before transferring any tuning conclusion.

## What the closed receipts already establish

- Both v160 arms were official v0.1.43, pristine revision `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`, using the same 32,768 token input IDs, binary hash `49025c6c…f3340f`, and same environment. They each requested `--pool-workers 5`, `--expert-cache-per-layer`, `--pcie-frac 0`, `--short-read 65536`, `--spec 8 --no-spec-split`, `--prefill 8`, `--adapt-swaps 0`, KV int8 / 32,768 resident cells, and the same profile. The receipt's actual route is `serial_read_windows8`, not batched prefill.
- `--expert-cache 128` was observed to initialize 144 slots / 281 MiB; `--expert-cache 512` initialized 624 / 1,218 MiB. The same route and arguments apart from cache size were used. This is one diagnostic point for each quota, not an optimality sweep. Reported LP5 and generated IDs differ; no task-quality parity conclusion is established.
- The 32,768 prompt has `short-read=65536`, so the eligible text is sent through the serial verifier-window route. `--prefill 8` does not make that input a batched-prefill measurement. The route is a conservative long-input path: prior source audits R206/R207/R208 found host-USM completion polling on the normal batched-prefill stager/PLE path, while R208/R219 document the stepped `read_windows` path and its synchronization boundary. Keep this route fixed for current comparisons. Lowering `--short-read` so the long text is dispatched to batched prefill is excluded until a separately qualified runtime path exists; do not use volatile polling or old GPU-hang handshakes.
- The control is costly by source geometry: 32,767 prompt positions at verifier width 8 require 4,096 windows, with 48 layer service boundaries per window. That is an explanation for why prompt route remains an independent target, not evidence a different route is safe or faster.
- The v160 JSON says `official_parameter_optimization_complete=false` and `full262144_runtime_qualified=false`. A configured max context of 262,144 is not a full-context run.

## Smallest useful comparisons not already in the pending candidate set

The registry/rounds already list cache-auto and worker-3 as pending candidates (R245), fixed prefill chunk brackets, installer auto, and width-4/8 route screens (R185/R208/R219/R225/R357/R367). Do not repeat those proposals here, or repeat worker-5/cache128/cache512 as if they were new candidates. The following two comparisons are distinct, source-backed screens; neither is a selected winner.

1. **Cache placement policy at a fixed byte budget:** compare the current `--expert-cache 128 --expert-cache-per-layer` against `--expert-cache 128` with the per-layer flag omitted. Keep profile, budget, reserve, run path, pool, prompt, KV, device/runtime, output budget, and everything else fixed. The existing 128/512 screen varies budget while holding the per-layer policy fixed; it does not test whether spreading the same budget globally or uniformly per layer better serves this prompt's layer-resolved routed experts. Record actual cache bytes, slots, profile fill, per-layer resident pairs, and CPU/device miss or hit counters separately for prompt and decode. Require same-request output/logit and normal fault/close gates. A change in placement may change CPU/GPU routing and numerical behavior, so keep any ID/LP5 divergence explicit; do not call a faster but divergent arm equivalent. Stop if the no-per-layer allocator's actual admitted bytes/reserve do not match the intended one-factor budget.

2. **Host core placement with the CPU pool held constant:** compare default `--host-core first` to `--host-core last`, while pinning the same `--pool-workers 5`, pool affinity (`all`), host participation, cache/profile, route, and every other setting. Upstream source says the host-core setting assigns the host thread to the first or last physical core and adjusts the worker-core set; it is a real control on Ryzen 5 5600X, unlike hybrid `p-cores` affinity. This is a low-cost topology/host-service hypothesis for the CPU-heavy stepped route, not a throughput prediction. Capture the source's startup topology (workers, assigned logical CPUs, host CPU and host drains), CPU miss service/segment times, prefill windows/tok/s, and decode tok/s separately. Use fresh processes and matched input; reject any setting that leaves the owner thread or workers unexpectedly unpinned or changes route/worker count. No evidence yet says first or last is better.

These should run only after the active owner/lock protocol permits GPU samples, using one exact safe build/runtime identity. Use a clean performance harness with instrumentation off for timing, and a separate correctness/diagnostic pass; do not reuse the validation/tracing timings as performance. Screen one factor at a time, then repeat a selected setting in multiple fresh processes and a held-out >=32K input. Record all samples, actual effective settings, memory headroom, exact prompt hash, output IDs/logprobs, fault results, and normal close. The prompt and decode decision must be reported separately, with no subtraction of overlapping spans.

## Deliberately excluded routes and changes

- The batched-prefill route or lowering `--short-read` for 32K+ text is not a safe candidate now. The prior source/runtime audits found host-polled host-USM stager/PLE completion in this route under unsupported host/shared-USM native atomics. `--no-pool`, fewer workers, a smaller chunk, or a positive PCIe share does not establish that synchronization is safe.
- Do not try volatile polling, the old GPU handshake route, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1` for mixed cache misses, or `STRATA_VERIFY_PIPE=1`; the measured safe route explicitly has stepped service, pipe off, host service on. A cache that happens to hit more experts is not proof that a different all-resident/doorbell route is safe.
- Do not combine cache policy, worker placement, and prefill route in one arm. A larger cache changes CPU misses, which changes the work available to the CPU pool. Worker placement changes CPU service and may affect both prompt and decode.

## Primary source evidence

All source claims below refer to the pristine v0.1.43 revision, not the selected integration revision `0691bcdf`.

- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` SHA-256 `8112c1808dc317e89d9635ad1b6e46b080fc16e67a0b2f63923d5231f355fa07`. CLI parser: `--pool-workers`, `--host-core`, `--pool-affinity`, `--prefill`, `--short-read`, cache policy, and adaptation options around lines 1748–1919. Pool construction and startup topology report at 4245–4260. Cache auto/per-layer sizing and allocation/fill at 4269–4794. `short_read` route selection at 9838–9844 and 10296–10320; `read_windows` loop at 9958–10008. The upstream code at this exact revision is [generate.cpp](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d/sycl/src/program/generate.cpp).
- `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp` SHA-256 `4b9b8ec1eeaabca0524a3a4aef39907ad90583e798d1e03a2ae1f6318e9105bc`. It reserves the selected host core and adjusts worker cores in `detect_cpu_topology` (lines 36–57); `HostCore::Last` moves the host to the last enumerated physical core and puts the previous host core into the worker set. The worker uses the host to drain jobs when enabled (line 695). [pool.cpp](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d/src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp).
- `include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp` SHA-256 `5f7e7ee3f48ce6505ad25975c320310e647551df3304a87052ce3c7e2b414936`. It documents core assignment and `host_works`; [pool.hpp](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d/include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp).
- Official reports consulted for completed-vs-pending controls and route safety: R185, R202, R206, R207, R208, R219, R225, R245, R254, R357, R358, R367. R245 lists cache-auto and worker-3 as pending; R254 documents per-layer policy/cache and adaptation effects; R208/R219/R225 bound safe long-prompt routes and width; R367 lists earlier chunk/worker/spec/cache searches. No report or registry status was changed.

## Evidence hashes

- `UPDATE_RESULTS-v160.md`: supplied results directory; read as received.
- `official-cache128-cache512-results-v160.json`: SHA-256 `68751ae3c46c7fe61fe88562fece7851e782d09ea8f3a753bd936e61b3e67fd5`.
- `pristine-official-full32k-results-v156.json`: SHA-256 `1f2948db5ba027e127f4c0c244047f9c8a8b9fdc92c25430c7b3292410b08f1c`.

## Limits

This is a read-only source/receipt audit. It neither ran candidates nor verified the runtime binary against the safe source-built LLVM package. The result is an incomplete measurement frontier, not a selected optimal configuration. A clean, matched run on the intended safe stack is still required before any claim that v0.1.43's settings are optimized for B570 or transferable to another runtime.
